question.text: Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations: \[ \mathbf{x}'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} -\dfrac{3}{5} & -\dfrac{4}{5} \\[2pt] \dfrac{1}{5} & -\dfrac{7}{5} \end{bmatrix} \mathbf{x}(t) + \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} \] A complementary solution to this system is given by \[ \mathbf{x}_c(t) = c_1 \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} e^{-t} + c_2 \left( t\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} \right) e^{-t}, \qquad c_1, c_2 \in\mathbb{R}. \] Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $\mathbf{x}(t) = \mathbf{x}_c(t) + \mathbf{x}_p(t),$ where $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution $\mathbf{x}_p(t).$
question.explanation:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = \mathbf{x}_c(t) + \mathbf{x}_p(t) \] where $\mathbf{x}_c(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term \[ \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix} \] of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is constant. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also constant, i.e. \[ \mathbf{x}_p(t) = \begin{bmatrix} a_1 \\ a_2 \end{bmatrix}, \] where $a_1,a_2$ are constants that are to be determined.

question.explanation:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = \mathbf{x}_c(t) + \mathbf{x}_p(t) \] where $\mathbf{x}_c(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term \[ e^{-4t} \begin{bmatrix} -14 \\ -27 \end{bmatrix} \] of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is exponential. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also exponential, i.e. \[ \mathbf{x}_p(t) = e^{-4t} \begin{bmatrix} a \\ b \end{bmatrix}, \] where $a,b$ are constants that are to be determined.

Calculating the derivative of $\mathbf{x}_p$ with respect to $t$ gives \[ \mathbf{x}'_p(t) = -4e^{-4t} \begin{bmatrix} a \\ b \end{bmatrix}. \]

To find the unknown constants, we substitute $\mathbf{x}_p$ and $\mathbf{x}'_p$ into our system:

\begin{align*} -4e^{-4t} \begin{bmatrix} a \\ b \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix} e^{-4t} \begin{bmatrix} a \\ b \end{bmatrix} + e^{-4t} \begin{bmatrix} -14 \\ -27 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] -4\begin{bmatrix} a \\ b \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} a \\ b \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -14 \\ -27 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} -4a \\ -4b \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3a \\ 5b \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -14 \\ -27 \end{bmatrix}\\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} -4a \\ -4b \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3a - 14 \\ 5b - 27 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} 3a - 14 = -4a \\[4pt] 5b - 27 = -4b \end{cases} \]

From the first equation, we get \[ 3a - 14 = -4a \qquad\Rightarrow\qquad a = 2. \]

From the second equation, we get \[ 5b - 27 = -4b \qquad\Rightarrow\qquad b = 3. \]

Therefore, the particular solution is \[ \mathbf{x}_p(t) = \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{e^{-4t}} \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\[3pt] \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{3} \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.text:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:
\[
\mathbf{x}'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{5}{3} & -\dfrac{8}{3} \\[2pt] -\dfrac{4}{3} & \dfrac{1}{3} \end{bmatrix} \mathbf{x}(t) + \begin{bmatrix} -6t^2 + \dfrac{41}{3}t - 8 \\[2pt] 3t^2 - \dfrac{13}{3}t + 5 \end{bmatrix}
\]
The complementary solution to this system is given by
\[
\mathbf{x}_c(t) = 
c_1\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} e^{-t} 
+ c_2\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} e^{3t},
\qquad c_1, c_2 \in\mathbb{R}.
\]
Then, the general solution of the system is

$\mathbf{x}(t) = \mathbf{x}_c(t) +\:\:$ [answer: 2; type: number; width: 30; margin-left: 2; margin-right: 2; buttons: frac;] $\:\: t^2 +\:\:$ $-1$ $\:\: t +\:\:$ [answer: 1; type: number; width: 30; margin-left: 2; margin-right: 2; buttons: frac;] .
$-1$ [answer: 3; type: number; width: 30; margin-left: 2; margin-right: 2; buttons: frac;] $-2$
question.explanation:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = \mathbf{x}_c(t) + \mathbf{x}_p(t) \] where $\mathbf{x}_c(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term \[ \begin{bmatrix} -6t^2 + \dfrac{41}{3}t - 8 \\ 3t^2 - \dfrac{13}{3}t + 5 \end{bmatrix} \] of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is polynomial of degree $2.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also polynomial of degree $2,$ i.e. \[ \mathbf{x}_p(t)= \begin{bmatrix} a_1 t^2 + b_1 t + c_1 \\ a_2 t^2 + b_2 t + c_2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} a_1 \\ a_2 \end{bmatrix} t^2 + \begin{bmatrix} b_1 \\ b_2 \end{bmatrix} t + \begin{bmatrix} c_1 \\ c_2 \end{bmatrix}, \] where $a_1,a_2, b_1,b_2,c_1,c_2$ are constants that are to be determined.

Calculating the derivative of $\mathbf{x}_p$ with respect to $t$ gives \[ \mathbf{x}'_p(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 2a_1 t + b_1 \\ 2a_2 t + b_2 \end{bmatrix}. \]

To find the unknown constants, we substitute $\mathbf{x}_p$ and $\mathbf{x}'_p$ into our system:

\begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix} 2a_1 t + b_1 \\ 2a_2 t + b_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac53 & -\dfrac83 \\ -\dfrac43 & \dfrac13 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} a_1 t^2 + b_1 t + c_1 \\ a_2 t^2 + b_2 t + c_2 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -6t^2 + \dfrac{41}{3}t - 8 \\ 3t^2 - \dfrac{13}{3}t + 5 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 2a_1 t + b_1 \\ 2a_2 t + b_2 \end{bmatrix}&= \begin{bmatrix} \left(\dfrac{5a_1-8a_2}{3}\right) t^2 + \left(\dfrac{5 b_1 - 8 b_2}{3}\right) t + \left(\dfrac{5 c_1 - 8 c_2}{3}\right) \\ \left(\dfrac{-4a_1 + a_2}{3}\right) t^2 + \left(\dfrac{-4 b_1 + b_2}{3}\right) t + \left(\dfrac{-4 c_1 + c_2}{3}\right) \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -6t^2 + \dfrac{41}{3}t - 8 \\ 3t^2 - \dfrac{13}{3}t + 5 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 0t^2 + 2a_1 t + b_1 \\ 0t^2 + 2a_2 t + b_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} \left(\dfrac{5a_1-8a_2-18}{3}\right) t^2 + \left(\dfrac{5 b_1 - 8 b_2+41}{3}\right) t + \left(\dfrac{5 c_1 - 8 c_2-24}{3}\right) \\ \left(\dfrac{-4a_1 + a_2+9}{3}\right) t^2 + \left(\dfrac{-4 b_1 + b_2-13}{3}\right) t + \left(\dfrac{-4 c_1 + c_2+15}{3}\right) \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding coefficients of like powers of $t,$ we get the following system: \[ \begin{cases} \dfrac{5a_1 - 8a_2-18}{3} = 0 \\[3pt] \dfrac{-4a_1 + a_2+9}{3} = 0 \\[3pt] \dfrac{5b_1 - 8b_2+41}{3} = 2a_1\\[3pt] \dfrac{-4b_1 + b_2-13}{3} = 2a_2 \\[3pt] \dfrac{5c_1 - 8c_2-24}{3} = b_1 \\[3pt] \dfrac{-4c_1 + c_2+15}{3} = b_2 \end{cases} \]

Solving the first and second equations, we get \[ a_1=2,\quad a_2=-1. \]

Substituting these into the second and third equations, and solving for $b_1$ and $b_2,$ we get

\[ b_1=-1,\quad b_2=3. \]

Finally, substituting these last two values into the fourth and sixth equations, and solving for $c_1$ and $c_2,$ we have

\[ c_1=1,\quad c_2=-2. \]

Therefore, the particular solution is \[ \mathbf{x}_p(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 2t^2 - t + 1 \\ -t^2 + 3t - 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{2} \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} t^2 + \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{3} \end{bmatrix} t + \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{1} \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}. \]

question.explanation:
We are told that the general solution to the system is \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1\begin{bmatrix} e^{2t} \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + c_2\begin{bmatrix} t e^{2t} \\ e^{2t} \end{bmatrix} + e^{-t} \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \] where $c_1,c_2$ are constants that are to be determined.

Next, we find the values of $c_1$ and $c_2.$ Substituting $t = 0$ into the general solution, we get the following: \begin{align*} \mathbf{x}(0) & = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] c_1 \begin{bmatrix} e^{2(0)} \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + c_2\begin{bmatrix} 0 \cdot e^{2(0)} \\ e^{2(0)} \end{bmatrix} + e^{-0} \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] c_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + c_2\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} c_1 \\ c_2 + 1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of linear equations: \[ \begin{cases} c_1 = 3 \\[3pt] c_2 + 1 = -2 \end{cases} \]

From the first equation, we have $c_1 = 3.$ From the second equation, we get $c_2 = -3.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{3} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} e^{2t} \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} - \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{3} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} t e^{2t} \\ e^{2t} \end{bmatrix} + e^{-t} \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

We are told that the general solution to the system is \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1\begin{bmatrix} e^t \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + c_2\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ e^{2t} \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} t^2 - t + 1 \\ 2t - 3 \end{bmatrix} \] where $c_1,c_2$ are constants that are to be determined.

Next, we find the values of $c_1$ and $c_2.$ Substituting $t = 0$ into the general solution, we get the following: \begin{align*} \mathbf{x}(0) & = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] c_1 \begin{bmatrix} e^0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + c_2\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ e^{2(0)} \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 0^2 - 0 + 1 \\ 2(0) - 3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] c_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + c_2\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} c_1 + 1 \\ c_2 - 3 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -5 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

So, we have the following system of linear equations: \[ \begin{cases} c_1 + 1 = 2 \\[3pt] c_2 - 3 = -5 \end{cases} \]

From the first equation, we get $c_1 = 1.$ From the second equation, we have $c_2 = -2.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{1} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} e^t \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} - \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{2} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ e^{2t} \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} t^2 - t + 1 \\ 2t - 3 \end{bmatrix}. \]
